# Provider fixtures

Every file under `github/`, `gitlab/`, `stripe/` and `generic/` is a request body replayed through
the real ingress route by `replay.test.ts` (spec 05 F72, spec 06 F79). `manifest.json` is the
provenance record of each one; `golden/` holds the expected outcome, canonical event, routing result
and rendered Slack, Lark, Teams and Discord payloads. Nothing here was captured from a live account.

## Provenance (read 2026-10-14)

| Provider | Where it came from | What is verbatim | What is not |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| GitHub | Examples in [octokit/webhooks `payload-examples/api.github.com`](https://github.com/octokit/webhooks/tree/aa80c24a3f55354465b8b1438d33dd5602956d0d/payload-examples/api.github.com) at commit `aa80c24` (GitHub-maintained; the source of the examples on [docs.github.com/en/webhooks/webhook-events-and-payloads](https://docs.github.com/en/webhooks/webhook-events-and-payloads)). The docs page itself was read to confirm the 25 MB cap and the `ghost` sender rule. | Every `documented` file. | Files marked `derived` in the manifest change named fields of one documented example (for example `workflow_run.conclusion`, `pull_request.merged`, `sender`). **UNVERIFIED** that the docs page renders byte-identical examples: its own inline example is partial. |
| GitLab | [docs.gitlab.com/user/project/integrations/webhook_events](https://docs.gitlab.com/user/project/integrations/webhook_events/), the page's Markdown source as served on 2026-10-14. | The JSON blocks for push, tag push, issue, merge request (action `open`) and pipeline (status `success`). | `derived` files change `object_attributes.action` or `status`. **UNVERIFIED**: the `X-Gitlab-Instance` value GitLab.com sends, and every pipeline status other than `success`. |
| Stripe | The documented Event object ([docs.stripe.com/api/events/object](https://docs.stripe.com/api/events/object)) and the resource examples in [stripe/openapi `fixtures3.json`](https://github.com/stripe/openapi/blob/master/openapi/fixtures3.json). | `plan.created.json` is the documented Event, unchanged. | The other Stripe files are **composed**: that Event with `type` set and `data.object` replaced by the documented example of the matching resource. **UNVERIFIED** that Stripe sends exactly that pairing, and the shape of `data.previous_attributes`. Several resource examples hold `null` where a real event has a value; the mapper reads them as absent. |
| Generic | Written by Noti to the contract in `docs/API.md`. | n/a | All of it: there is no provider to capture. |

Documented GitHub examples that carry no `installation` block (or a placeholder one) have the
installation id of the test tenant set at replay time (`rig.encode`); the file on disk stays as
published.

## What the replay asserts

For every manifest entry, in a fresh fake D1, signed with a secret generated at run time:

- the outcome (`delivered`, `ignored`, `lifecycle`, `ping`) matches the manifest and the golden;
- the canonical event equals the golden, validates, and is what the queue message was derived from;
- for GitHub, each of six integrations (no filter; branch allow-list; bots excluded; actor allow-list;
  drafts excluded; label include) delivered or recorded a filter reason;
- for the entries marked `render` in the manifest (a representative eight), the Slack, Lark, Teams
  and Discord payloads equal the golden; the destination suites own rendering for the rest.

Negative cases (truncated body, forged or missing signature, wrong content type, oversize, unsupported
event, unknown or disabled endpoint, a reused id, a stale timestamp) are in
`tests/conformance/conformance.test.ts` and `tests/github/ingress-contract.test.ts`; the oversize body
is generated at run time rather than committed.

## Changing a golden

Goldens change only on an explicit run, and the diff is the review:

```sh
UPDATE_GOLDEN=1 npm test -- tests/fixtures/replay.test.ts
git diff tests/fixtures/golden
```

A missing golden fails the suite; it is never created implicitly, and the update is refused when
`CI` is set.

## Adding a fixture

1. Copy the example as published into the provider folder; add a manifest entry with its source URL,
   read date, `provenance`, `expect` and, if it is derived, the exact `derive` change.
2. Run the update command above and read every line of the new golden.
3. Check it for personal data and secrets: `hygiene.test.ts` scans every file here for token shapes,
   bidirectional controls and any email address outside the providers' published examples. Secrets
   used to sign requests are generated by the test rig and never appear in a file.
4. A real capture is sensitive until sanitised: the working copy is as sensitive as the repository.
   Replace tenant, repository and person data with example values before it is committed.
